topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private fit
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-23 16:00 UTC — duration 46m — attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Aria Chen (Redwood SE) — Samir Patel (CTO, Helios Mesh), Maya Green (Lead ML Eng), Oliver Royce (DevOps), Nina Wong (PM)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Samir, Maya, Oliver, Nina, and on our side Diego and Aria. Do you all see my screen?
[00:08] Samir Patel: Yep, seeing it. Thanks for the invite. We're tight on time so want to focus on time-to-first-inference and security things.
[00:15] Lena Park: Great. High level: Redwood offers hosted API for fastest time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private/VPC options for strict data controls. Today we can talk pilot scope — free credits, quickstart, and benchmarks.
[00:30] Maya Green: Quick question up front — we are evaluating whether to prototype on hosted and then move to dedicated, or go straight to private due to some PII-ish data. Our regulatory folks may push for VPC.
[00:42] Diego Morales: Totally fair. From a technical POV we normally recommend hosted for the first sprint because you can get to first token in hours with self-serve credits. Then if you hit production traffic or need isolation we help map to Dedicated or Private. There are tradeoffs on latency vs cost and isolation.
[00:58] Oliver Royce: When you say "hours", what does that practically mean? We want an endpoint we can call from our preexisting infra and run a 1k request bench by EOW.
[01:10] Aria Chen: In practice, for an eval you sign up, we issue a credit allocation for the pilot, we share a quickstart repo and a Postman/SDK example. You can do the first call in less than an hour; getting a production-like benchmark might take a day or two depending on prompt prep and payload size.
[01:28] Nina Wong: Who do we talk to about the free credits? Our budget team needs a formal note.
[01:33] Lena Park: I'll send a formal credits allocation note and a pilot proposal after this call. It will list the credit quantity and what that roughly translates to in tokens.
[01:39] Samir Patel: Cool. On security, we have three main blockers: SSO for the console, audit logs, and KMS integration.
[01:49] Diego Morales: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC in the Console, and the Private deployment can plug into your KMS/HSM. Audit logs are available — we can share the schema. For hosted we offer customer-level audit trails and can provide SOC 2 Type II docs.
[02:06] Maya Green: Are there limitations on retention for hosted logs vs private? Our compliance requires 12 months of immutable logs.
[02:13] Aria Chen: Hosted has configurable retention windows; for 12 months we'd likely recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment or an add-on log retention package. We'll note that in the security doc.
[02:26] Lena Park: Let's pivot to success criteria — what does Helios Mesh want to learn from the pilot?
[02:33] Samir Patel: Three things: 1) realistic latency numbers for our typical payload (avg 400 tokens), 2) cost per 1k responses at our QPS target (10-20 qps), 3) an integration proof that respects our network constraints.
[02:47] Diego Morales: Great. For latency, we typically provide model profiles — which model family are you planning to use? Open models are fine for most of our customers.
[02:55] Maya Green: We're testing a finetuned Llama variant internally — roughly 7B parameters quantized to 8-bit. Will Redwood host quantized models?
[03:06] Diego Morales: Yes, we support quantized variants. Note that quantization changes latency and memory tradeoffs. Also, we do kernel selection and some attention optimizations — you might see different perf between hosted and Dedicated GPUs.
[03:19] Oliver Royce: Do you expose KV cache or is that managed inside the runtime? We have conversational flows that rely on efficient caching.
[03:27] Aria Chen: We have automatic KV caching and prefix caching in the runtime; it's managed but configurable. Sometimes transcriptions show "K-V cash" in notes, but it's a KV cache.
[03:39] Samir Patel: Haha, noted. For throughput at 10-20 QPS, how do we think about batching vs latency?
[03:46] Diego Morales: Batching reduces unit cost but can increase tail latency. For interactive flows we recommend small batch sizes with autoscaling; for high-throughput async workloads, Dedicated pools with larger batching are cost-efficient. We'll include suggested autoscale configs in the benchmark checklist.
[04:03] Maya Green: About data residency — our EU customers' data needs to stay in eu-west. Hosted regioning supports that?
[04:10] Lena Park: Yes, hosted supports region pins; Private obviously offers full control. If residency is critical, Dedicated in an EU region or Private are typical.
[04:19] Nina Wong: What's the billing model for the pilot? Are credits consumed by tokens? Any flat fees?
[04:25] Lena Park: Pilot credits map to token consumption and are consumable against generation and embedding units depending on the workload. No mandatory flat fee for a short pilot; if you want dedicated capacity reserved, that's a contract.
[04:36] Oliver Royce: We want to run a benchmark that looks like production: concurrent users hitting a chat endpoint, about 400 token average. We'll need a test harness.
[04:45] Diego Morales: We'll share a benchmark harness (python script + k6 snippet) and a micro-benchmark spreadsheet to record latency p50/p95/p99 and cost.
[04:55] Samir Patel: On SSO details — we use Okta. How granular is the RBAC in Redwood Console?
[05:02] Aria Chen: You can map SAML attributes to roles and set per-route permissions. For tighter controls, Private gives you the most granular network policies.
[05:12] Maya Green: Are there any limitations when we bring our own model? Can we host customer models on Redwood Hosted?
[05:19] Diego Morales: For hosted we can host selected customer models behind a private model namespace — there are onboarding steps and some approvals for copyrighted or sensitive model artifacts. For Dedicated and Private, you can bring your model and pin it.
[05:31] Nina Wong: If we need to run on prem later, what's the path?
[05:35] Lena Park: We have a Private deployment offering that can be customer-managed on VPC or on-prem. Usually customers do hosted -> Dedicated -> Private, but some go hosted -> Private if compliance requires.
[05:47] Samir Patel: Okay. Let's sketch timeline: we'd like to start proof-of-concept next week and finish bench by April 6. Doable?
[05:55] Diego Morales: Tight but doable — if you share prompts and sample payload today or tomorrow we can spin up the hosted pilot and run initial benches in 5 business days.
[06:06] Maya Green: We can share a small prompt set and 200 sample payloads by tomorrow.
[06:11] Lena Park: Perfect. I'll follow up with a pilot proposal and credits. Diego will send the benchmark pack.
[06:19] [Chatter/brief off-topic about conference logistics]
[07:02] Oliver Royce: A couple of specific technical notes: 1) our payloads include attachments (base64) occasionally — any size limits? 2) we need TLS mTLS inbound for some internal calls.
[07:13] Aria Chen: Attachments are fine if within request size limits — we'll share exact limits in the API docs. For mTLS, Hosted doesn't provide inbound mTLS termination to your private network; Private/VPC can accommodate mutual TLS or peered connections.
[07:28] Samir Patel: Also, any way to route to lower-cost model variants automatically if the primary model is at capacity?
[07:34] Diego Morales: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or to a lower-cost quantized variant based on policy. We'll show that in the routing examples.
[07:44] Maya Green: One more — we use a proprietary vector store; do you integrate with external embedding endpoints or do we have to ingest?
[07:51] Aria Chen: You can host embeddings via our API and choose to store vectors in your store; we also support export hooks. We'll include embedding best practices.
[08:02] [Pause — quick background noise, transcription picks up 'uh' and 'huh']
[08:17] Nina Wong: Okay I think we have enough. Could you repeat the immediate action items?
[08:22] Lena Park: Sure — 1) Lena: send pilot proposal, credits, and security links by Wednesday 2026-03-25. 2) Diego: benchmark pack and micro-benchmark spreadsheet by Friday 2026-03-27. 3) Maya: share prompt set and 200 sample payloads by 2026-03-24. 4) Customer to confirm SOC2 contact and SSO owner by 2026-03-30.
[08:44] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Who should we Cc on the security thread?
[08:48] Aria Chen: CC me and Diego and I'll loop in our security eng. I'll also attach the SOC2 and architecture doc — note sometimes names are slightly different in generated docs — but we'll make sure the right files are in the link.
[09:00] Lena Park: Any other blockers?
[09:03] Oliver Royce: Not from infra. We'll start prepping the prompt set.
[09:06] Maya Green: Happy with next steps.
[09:08] Lena Park: Great — we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
[09:12] [Meeting closes — small hellos and hangup noises]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings ("K-V cash" for KV cache), names sometimes merged (Aria/Diego overlap), filler words preserved.

References shared: Pilot proposal template (link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-proposal/CRM-89321), Benchmark harness repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness), Security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2)
